summary: The market data pool opens a second connection when the first is full (one instrument each here): its ticks reach its own client only; the broker closes it and refuses it while the first connection keeps streaming, then it reconnects and subscribes its instrument again.

notes: The session's pool is 1,000 instruments a connection and 2 connections (broker_runtime::pool_limits; rule life-d1-d8, D4); the case lowers it to one instrument a connection, so two instruments open the second connection. The web's pool opens its next connection at 1,000 a connection too, up to 3.
The web replay runs one adapter for the whole pool, and every frame here is a full packet of one instrument, so which connection carried it does not change the web's output.

deviations.reason: HDFC Securities sends lastTradeTime in epoch seconds (the web's own test pairs lastTradeTime 1700000000 with packetTimestamp 1700000000000); the web sends it unconverted as ltt, a docs key that is epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md). The desktop converts it to ms (investright::trade_time_ms). Lead decision: ltt in seconds -> ms, web defect (wrong unit).

A cash equity's packet carries no OI (proto3 writes oi 0); the web sends that 0 as oi and open_interest instead of leaving them out (web openalgo#2376). The desktop counts OI on the derivative segments only. Lead decision: web zeros for values the stream did not send are left out, web defect.
